tools.name: categories
tools.description: Read the user’s categories by space and kind. Use these exact names in record, plan and split. Manage categories in Bluu.

tools.name: budgets
tools.description: The limits the user set per category, with how much is spent and what is left. `is_exceeded` flags one they have gone over. A budget added from this chat carries a `ref`: with it, `plan` can change or delete it.

tools.name: goals
tools.description: What the user is saving toward: target, how much is set aside, progress and any deadline. Name a `goal` to answer "when will I get there?" tools.name: commitments
tools.description: Everything the user is committed to paying: recurring subscriptions and upcoming reminders, soonest first. This answers "what do I owe" and "what is charging next". A reminder or subscription added from this chat carries a `ref`: with it, `plan` can change or delete it.

tools.name: overview
tools.description: A short read on one space right now: what is coming up to pay, budgets that are over, how goals are pacing, and one thing worth noticing. Use it for "how am I doing?" and check-ins. Answer with the conclusions, then offer the link — the full picture is in Bluu.

tools.name: what_if
tools.description: When the user would reach a savings target they do not have as a goal yet: "how long to save 6 million for a trip at 500 thousand a month?". Give the target and, if they said them, the monthly amount and what they already have (without a monthly amount Bluu uses what they have left over each month).

tools.name: people
tools.description: Who owes the user and whom they owe, split requests waiting for their answer, and what they share with someone over time. Names only — Bluu never hands out another person's contact details.

tools.name: open_in_bluu
tools.description: A link that opens Bluu on the right screen — for "where do I…?", for anything better seen than read (charts, the full list, simulations), and for what is only done in Bluu (scanning a receipt, settings, devices, deleting). Ask with `question` in the user's words, or name a `screen`.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "spaces" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "what_if" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: goals, record, invite, invest, statements · Private data: spaces, spending, categories, people, record, split, invite, invest, confirm, statements · Public sink: people, split, invite · Destructive: spending, budgets, commitments, record, plan, invest.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: goals, record, invite, invest, statements · Private data: spaces, spending, categories, people, record, split, invite, invest, confirm, statements · Public sink: people, split, invite · Destructive: spending, budgets, commitments, record, plan, invest

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
